defs: Assigning each token a part-of-speech tag; a sequence-labelling task.
Word class that readily admits new words (N, V, Adj, Adv).
Small fixed class of function words (prepositions, determiners, pronouns, auxiliaries).
45 English tags (NN, NNS, VBD, DT, IN, TO, …).
Tag each word with its most common training tag (~92%).
States with π and transition matrix A; next state depends only on current.
Hidden states with transitions A, emissions B and start π.
Each word depends only on its own tag.
takeaways: Context can override a word's usual tag.
confused: P(tag | previous tag) vs P(word | tag).
Observed states vs hidden states emitting observations.
Most types unambiguous; many tokens ambiguous.
Model P(w, t) vs model P(t | w) directly (MEMM, M7).
recall.minute: POS tagging assigns tags to tokens: the/DT lead/NN paint/NN is/VBZ unsafe/JJ. Uses: lemmatisation, parsing, NER, MT, TTS. Open classes (N, V, Adj, Adv) grow; closed classes (prepositions, determiners, pronouns, auxiliaries) don't, so unknown words are open-class. Penn has 45 tags (NN, NNS, NNP, VB, VBD, VBG, VBZ, DT, JJ, IN incl. subordinating conjunctions, TO); 'The/DT grand/JJ jury/NN commented/VBD on/IN a/DT number/NN of/IN other/JJ topics/NNS'. UD has 17. Ambiguity: I can can the can (MD VB NN); back JJ/NN/RB/VB; most-frequent baseline ~92%, HMMs ~97%. 45⁵ ≈ 1.85 × 10⁸ sequences. Markov chain: π, A; warm×4 = 0.0432. HMM adds emissions B; joint Π P(tᵢ|tᵢ₋₁)P(wᵢ|tᵢ): the dog barks = 0.06 × 0.00024 = 1.44 × 10⁻⁵; decode argmax P(w|t)P(t). Estimates by counts: P(NN|DT) = 600/1000, P(is|VBZ) = 300/500; toy start DT 2/3, P(NNS|DT) = 1/2, P(the|DT) = 3/4, P(exam|NN) = 1. Race: VB 0.83 × 0.0027 × 0.00012 = 2.7 × 10⁻⁷ vs NN 0.00047 × 0.0012 × 0.00057 = 3.2 × 10⁻¹⁰.
